root_cause.text: In `drivers/nvmem/zynqmp_nvmem.c` (`zynqmp_efuse_access()`), the driver used the size of the `bytes` variable itself (`sizeof(bytes)`) instead of the requested transfer length `bytes` when allocating/freeing the DMA buffer, and also copied the wrong amount into a local `value`, causing undersized buffer access and possible memory corruption.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `dma_alloc_coherent(dev, sizeof(bytes), ...)` to `dma_alloc_coherent(dev, bytes, ...)` and `dma_free_coherent(dev, sizeof(bytes), ...)` to `dma_free_coherent(dev, bytes, ...)`, and replaces `memcpy(&value, val, bytes)` with `memcpy(&value, val, sizeof(value))`, while the CVE states the “buffer size used in dma allocation and memcpy is wrong” and “can lead to undersized DMA buffer access and possible memory corruption.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Use an unsigned temporary for eFuse word access to avoid signedness-related data handling bugs.
intent_record.what: The local variable `value` in `zynqmp_efuse_access()` was changed from type `int` to `unsigned int`; no other code in the hunk was modified.
intent_record.how: This changes how the temporary word-sized value is represented during eFuse access, preventing signed interpretation of what is presumably an unsigned hardware data value and avoiding sign-related issues when storing or handling the read/write word.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix EFUSE write handling by copying the full value size before checking PUF-specific bits.
intent_record.what: In the EFUSE write path of zynqmp_efuse_access(), the memcpy destination remains &value but the copy length changes from bytes to sizeof(value).
intent_record.how: This makes the code always copy the full width of value instead of a variable byte count, preventing partial initialization or truncation when evaluating the written data for the PUF-related mask check.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the DMA buffer allocation to use the requested byte count instead of the size of the size variable.
intent_record.what: In the call to dma_alloc_coherent(), the size argument was changed from sizeof(bytes) to bytes.
intent_record.how: The allocation now uses the actual buffer size requested by the variable bytes instead of the size of the bytes variable itself, which ensures the DMA buffer is allocated with the correct length at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the DMA buffer free call to use the correct allocation size in `zynqmp_efuse_access()`.
intent_record.what: In the cleanup path of `zynqmp_efuse_access()`, the `dma_free_coherent()` call was changed from passing `sizeof(bytes)` as the allocation size to passing `bytes`.
intent_record.how: This makes the DMA buffer release use the same size that was presumably used for the allocation, ensuring the coherent buffer is freed with the correct length and avoiding a size mismatch in the deallocation path.

Fix the DMA buffer free call to use the correct allocation size in `zynqmp_efuse_access()`.

relevance_review.reason: The change is about using an unsigned temporary to avoid signedness issues, while the vulnerability root cause is an incorrect buffer size/copy length bug in DMA handling. It does not address the sizeof(bytes) misuse or the associated memory corruption.
The change is about EFUSE write handling and PUF-specific bit checks, not the DMA buffer sizing bug in zynqmp_efuse_access() where sizeof(bytes) was used instead of the requested transfer length.

The group directly addresses the root cause by fixing the DMA buffer allocation to use the requested transfer length instead of sizeof(bytes), which is one of the core bugs leading to undersized buffer access and potential memory corruption.

The root cause is incorrect use of sizeof(bytes) instead of the requested length in zynqmp_efuse_access(), leading to DMA buffer size misuse and potential corruption. This group directly fixes the DMA buffer free/allocation size handling in that same function, so it addresses part of the vulnerability root cause.

candidates.rationale: This allocates the DMA buffer using the size of the local variable 'bytes' rather than the requested transfer length 'bytes', creating an undersized buffer and enabling out-of-bounds access/corruption.
This frees the DMA buffer with the same incorrect size used for allocation, reflecting the underlying size-mismatch bug in the access path and tied to the same root cause.

The copy operation uses the requested byte count against a buffer that was allocated with only sizeof(bytes) bytes, so this statement can read past the undersized DMA buffer and contribute to memory corruption.

vuln_statements.explanation: This allocation uses sizeof(bytes) instead of the requested transfer length bytes, creating an undersized DMA buffer and enabling out-of-bounds access.
This copies bytes from the DMA buffer even though the buffer was allocated using only sizeof(bytes), so it can read past the end of the undersized buffer and corrupt memory.
This frees the DMA buffer with the same incorrect size used for allocation, reflecting the size-mismatch bug in the vulnerable access path.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in `zynqmp_efuse_access()`. The snippet allocates and frees the DMA buffer with `sizeof(bytes)` instead of the requested transfer length `bytes`: `data = dma_alloc_coherent(dev, sizeof(bytes), &dma_buf, GFP_KERNEL);` and later `dma_free_coherent(dev, sizeof(bytes), data, dma_buf);`. Since `bytes` is a `size_t`, `sizeof(bytes)` is just the size of the variable (typically 8), not the number of bytes requested, which matches the root cause described. The code also copies `bytes` into a local `int value` for the PUF write check via `memcpy(&value, val, bytes);`, which can overflow `value` when `bytes` is larger than `sizeof(int)`. There is no fix present in this function body: no allocation sized by `bytes`, no bounds check before `memcpy(&value, val, bytes)`, and the wrong-sized free mirrors the wrong-sized allocation.
